A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching authors and Sections 1–8. Their text, equations, nine figures and two tables support comparison. Both end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: v2 surveys existing research. Empirical observations are attributed to cited studies; its mathematical examples and illustrative or adapted figures do not establish original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 remains a survey without original experiments, simulations or data analyses. Its additions summarize theoretical results and applications from other works.

M1.justification: The architectural group actions, mathematical examples and optimization procedures are retained. Added references discuss existing methods rather than introduce or revise a proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts dataset-based training or evaluation. New mentions of MoE, long-tail recognition and dataset-size recovery expand literature coverage, without adding evaluated data or tasks.

E2.justification: No empirical baseline comparison is introduced. Table 2 retains ENorm, Weight Balancing, the same teleportation variants and Goldstone-GD as a catalogue of prior algorithms.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an original evaluation protocol. No experimental splits, metrics, training budgets or testing procedures are added or revised.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests or empirical case analyses are added. The existing loss-landscape and conservation-law illustrations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for original results. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: No empirical values, rankings or evaluated result entries change. Existing performance observations attributed to cited studies are retained; additions discuss theory and applications without reporting additional evaluation outcomes.

T1.justification: Sections 2.4 and 5.1 add cited theoretical results on completeness of MoE gating symmetries and conservation laws for transformer attention. Existing definitions, Proposition 2.5 and mathematical derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: surveying parameter-space symmetry and connecting it to loss landscapes, optimization and learning dynamics. No new primary contribution is claimed.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 updates the boundary of known conservation-law completeness beyond matrix factorization. Sections 4.1 and 7.3 broaden the discussion of teleportation applications and scalability, while Section 3.3 drops the explanation of compatibility with pruning, quantization and distillation.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware and code/data access disclosures do not change. Section 7.3 cites additional implementation approaches without supplying accompanying procedural or reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Adds references on recurrent-network symmetry, MoE identifiability, attention conservation laws, dataset-size recovery and teleportation applications. Numerous other edits update existing references to published versions, such as Grigsby et al. from 2022 to 2025; the survey's overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify loss composition, introduce the permutation example earlier, rename Section 2.3 to 'Relaxed Definitions of Symmetry,' and update acknowledgements. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The document-wide conversion to TMLR formatting redesigns the title and author block, adds running publication headers, changes typography and text width, and extensively resizes or relocates figures and tables. The same nine figures and two tables remain, with additional annotation-layout revisions in Figures 4 and 9.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the survey's account of established theory by adding MoE identifiability and updating Section 5.1's uncertainty about completeness beyond matrix factorization with cited attention-layer results. Specific application references also improve its usefulness. The loss of the compression-context sentence in Section 3.3 is limited and does not outweigh these modest gains.
